title: Kiss Kiss Bang Bang — main titles
description: Pulp-noir paper-cut silhouettes of LA: chain-link fences, freeways, a falling woman under a full moon, blood spatter over typeset novel pages. Limited palette of cream, black and blood red with condensed sans credits set into the scenery. Flat layers slide and wipe in a Saul Bass lineage.
why_top_tier: A three-colour graphic system executed with total consistency; every transition is a graphic match, and the type sits in the composition rather than over it.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Warner Bros. / Silver Pictures

title: Catch Me If You Can — main titles
description: Stamp-printed 1960s silhouettes chase each other through airports, pools and stairwells built from flat colour fields and thin vertical lines. Credits are set in a clean geometric sans that the characters walk past and hide behind. Palette flips scene by scene (sky blue, mustard, pink, green on black).
why_top_tier: Rubber-stamp textures and a strict vertical-line grid turn a cat-and-mouse chase into pure graphic choreography; a benchmark for 2D title design.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright DreamWorks Pictures

title: The Crown — main titles
description: Extreme macro CG of molten gold and silver slowly crystallising into the St Edward's crown, lit from a single soft source against near-black smoke. Tiny small-caps serif credits float in the negative space. Slow, weighty camera moves and shallow depth of field.
why_top_tier: Material rendering and lighting at jewellery-photography level; restraint in palette and type makes the metal the only subject.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Left Bank Pictures / Sony Pictures Television / Netflix

title: Severance — main titles
description: Surreal soft-body CG: a protagonist duplicated, melting into black goo, stranded on a white snowfield of desks and coffee mugs. Clinical white and teal office palette, small Helvetica-like credits with hairline rules. Dreamlike slow motion and morphing.
why_top_tier: Emmy-winning sequence whose simulation, sculpting and art direction turn corporate banality into body horror with immaculate compositional control.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Apple TV+ / Fifth Season

title: Westworld — main titles
description: Ivory-white robotic arms 3D-print sinew, a player piano and a horse and rider against black, ending on the Vitruvian host in a ring. Monochrome palette with milky subsurface materials and thin wide-tracked credits.
why_top_tier: Flawless material, light and macro camera work; a monochrome CG piece where every shot is a sculpture.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright HBO

title: Stranger Things — main titles
description: Glowing red ITC Benguiat letterforms slide past each other in extreme close-up on pure black, with subtle film grain and light bloom, until they lock into the logo. Credits in small white caps.
why_top_tier: A purely typographic sequence that builds tension from nothing but letter edges, kerning and glow; widely imitated.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Netflix

title: Marvel's Jessica Jones — main titles
description: Painterly, smeared noir vignettes of New York: silhouettes in doorways, windows and alleys rendered as streaked purple and amber brushwork with glitchy horizontal drags. Ends on a distressed blue logo.
why_top_tier: Merges David Mack's watercolour painting with motion smears so it feels like an illustration coming to life; distinctive and highly crafted.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Marvel / Netflix

title: Halt and Catch Fire — main titles
description: Abstract red-on-red electronic imagery: scan lines, pixel blocks, a glowing chip and a red circle, built from analogue video feedback. Small serif credits.
why_top_tier: Distils the birth of the PC into a minimal circuit-light language; tight rhythm cut to a synth score.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright AMC

title: Lemony Snicket's A Series of Unfortunate Events — end titles
description: Gothic storybook shadow-puppet cut-outs: a little boat on paper waves, a giant eye of interlocking cogs, spindly trees and silhouetted villains in sepia, grey and olive. Credits in classical serif.
why_top_tier: Edward Gorey-like paper-cut storybook animation with real tactile depth; the template for "dark children's book" motion.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Paramount Pictures / DreamWorks

title: The Incredibles — end titles
description: Flat 1960s spy-graphic animation: magenta and red silhouettes, musical staves, a car in red against black, bold italic sans credits integrated into the action.
why_top_tier: A loving pastiche of mid-century graphic design with superb limited-palette animation timed to the score.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Disney / Pixar

title: Semi-Permanent Sydney 2014 — opening titles
description: Speaker names and monograms built from exploding teal pigment and dust over a dark blueprint grid. Bold condensed type and ampersands materialise out of powder clouds.
why_top_tier: Real powder simulation fused with crisp typographic construction; a conference title with the finish of a feature film.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Semi-Permanent / MK12

title: Semi-Permanent Sydney 2019 — opening titles
description: Psychedelic CG vignettes on the theme "Truth": melting heads, marbled liquid in electric blue, purple and coral, glowing reliquaries, with outlined display type for speaker names.
why_top_tier: Each speaker card is its own art piece yet the palette and type system hold it together; a showcase of Elastic's design range.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Semi-Permanent / Elastic

title: OFFF Milano / Digital Design Days 2017 — titles
description: Art Deco golden machinery: kaleidoscopic gold geometric mandalas, clockwork-like mechanisms and gilded figures with custom Deco display lettering. Warm gold-on-black with glints and bokeh.
why_top_tier: Ornamental, guilloché-like precision in CG gold; custom typography and symmetry give it a luxury-watch level of finish.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright OFFF / Digital Design Days / Onur Senturk

title: FITC Tokyo 2015 — titles
studio: Ash Thorp, Michael Rigley, Nicolas Girard
description: A modular tile system of neon pixel glyphs, Latin and katakana letterforms, stripes and grids in pink, cyan, lime and violet on dark navy. Letters assemble from grid cells and scanning bars.
why_top_tier: Four custom alphabets driven by one grid; a textbook pattern/tile system for a design conference, tightly animated.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright FITC / the artists

title: Blanc Festival 2015 — titles
description: Bold flat-colour character animation: flowers, leaves, rubbery limbs and faces in coral, cobalt, mint and yellow, ending on a neon "Blanc Voyeur Club" sign. Hand-drawn shapes morph rhythmically.
why_top_tier: Joyful festival opener with flawless shape morphing and a confident illustrative palette.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Blanc Festival / Olga Capdevila

title: Da Vinci's Demons — main titles
description: Leonardo-style sepia ink sketches, codex handwriting and construction lines animate over clouds, domes and figures; ink splashes transition between scenes. Desaturated violet-grey and parchment palette with classical serif credits.
why_top_tier: Hand-drawn ink line work tracked into CG space; the ink-and-paper texture is the motion language.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Starz

title: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse — end titles
description: Comic-book halftones, misregistered CMYK, spray-paint textures and hand-lettered credits in violent yellow, magenta, blue and green. Spiders multiply into psychedelic radial patterns.
why_top_tier: Print-process artefacts turned into animation language; dense yet perfectly readable.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Sony Pictures Animation

title: Thank You for Smoking — main titles
description: Each credit is set as a vintage cigarette-pack design: crests, sunbursts, palm trees and stripes with period lettering in red, cream, blue and green. The camera pans across pack surfaces.
why_top_tier: Pitch-perfect packaging typography; dozens of bespoke lockups each authentic to an era.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Fox Searchlight

title: Mad Men — main titles
description: A black silhouette man falls past glass skyscrapers papered with 1960s ads, ending reclined on a sofa. Flat graphic silhouette over desaturated photographic reflections; small red sans credits.
why_top_tier: One iconic idea executed with economy; the silhouette-in-reflection compositing is still a reference.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright AMC / Lionsgate

title: Cosmos: A Spacetime Odyssey — main titles
description: Science-documentary CG: lunar craters, a human eye, a nautilus shell, a spiral galaxy, DNA, nebula, ending on the spaced CO S M O S wordmark inside an iris. Deep blue and amber palette.
why_top_tier: Seamless scale-jumping from cells to galaxies with scientific plausibility and an orchestral pace.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Fox / National Geographic

title: Game of Thrones — main titles
description: A clockwork map: cities of gears and wooden cogs rise out of a parchment map under an armillary sphere sun. Brass, stone and parchment palette with engraved serif credits.
why_top_tier: A map that literally builds itself; mechanical modelling and warm lighting at the highest level.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright HBO

title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo — main titles
description: Glossy black oil-like CG bodies, cables and flowers erupt and melt; one burst of orange fire breaks the monochrome. Small white credits.
why_top_tier: Liquid-surface rendering and art direction that is still unmatched for "black on black" CG.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Columbia Pictures

title: The Adventures of Tintin — main titles
description: Flat silhouette chase through ports, streets and docks in teal, orange, burgundy and olive. Tintin and Snowy run past lamps and ships; serif credits in-scene.
why_top_tier: Ligne-claire silhouettes and graphic spatial jumps; a storybook adventure in pure flat design.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Paramount / Columbia Pictures

title: Vertigo — main titles
description: Close-ups of an eye tinted red give way to Lissajous/spirograph spirals in green, violet and red on black, generated with John Whitney's mechanical analog computer. Slab serif credits.
why_top_tier: The origin of computer-generated motion graphics; hypnotic guilloché-like curves that still read as contemporary.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Paramount / Universal

title: The Boxtrolls — end titles
description: Scratchy ink-drawn characters and cobblestone cityscapes with watercolour washes; credits in hand-drawn serif lettering woven into the drawings.
why_top_tier: Loose pen-and-ink storybook illustration animated with great charm and lettering craft.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright LAIKA / Focus Features

title: J.P. Morgan Payments — creative expression
description: Warm ivory and gold CG: glass discs, coin stacks and a translucent card showing $2.45M travel through a minimal diagrammatic flow on a cream ground.
why_top_tier: Abstracts payment rails into a tactile, premium object language; flawless material and restraint for a fintech brand.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright JPMorgan Chase & Co.

title: Coinbase: System Update
description: An entirely terminal-style film: white monospaced code, ASCII particle drawings and glyph grids on Coinbase blue, morphing into characters, coins and data fields.
why_top_tier: Builds a whole fintech campaign from one generative ASCII constraint, with surprising warmth.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Coinbase

title: Osko — launch
description: A fast-payments service introduced via cute 3D and flat 2D vignettes: IOU sticky notes on a fridge, cars, golfers, everyday objects on soft grey grounds.
why_top_tier: Makes instant bank payments human with charming character design and crisp object animation.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright BPAY Group / Osko

title: Wealthsimple Trade — app launch
description: Soft-matte 3D icons in pastel circles: a steering wheel with UI arrows, a plug, a retro monitor, a portal of shares, on peach and grey grounds.
why_top_tier: Clean modernist 3D iconography turns trading concepts into a coherent object system.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Wealthsimple

title: Hermès — animated campaign
description: Circus animals, horseshoes and pattern-bands drawn in a silk-scarf style on deep Hermès red with tulip ornaments; later shots become dense op-art patterns.
why_top_tier: Translates the house's scarf illustration tradition into motion with print-level detail.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Hermès

title: A Tiffany Holiday
description: A CG dream journey through New York and a canyon: a bird flies past a vintage clock face, aerial city streets, a lit stage, a table set with crystal.
why_top_tier: Cinematic lighting and camera with luxury-film polish.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Tiffany & Co.

title: Calm — Sleep visual system
description: Soft gradient illustrations of sleepers, glowing moons and breathing light forms in lilac, peach and blue; airbrushed shapes ripple slowly.
why_top_tier: A sleep brand system whose slowness and grain are the content; calm motion done with real finesse.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Calm.com

title: Goodbooks — Metamorphosis
description: Kafka's Metamorphosis in loose brush-and-ink drawings with teal and mustard washes on paper; a man's face, an insect eye and sunglasses morph in black ink.
why_top_tier: Hand-drawn ink animation with expressive line boil; a frequently awarded charity piece.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Goodbooks / BUCK

title: BBC Two — idents
description: Textured toy-like 3D blocks, cylinders and foam shapes in teal, coral and silver tumble across a pegboard, settling with the BBC Two wordmark.
why_top_tier: Tactile materials and satisfying physics in a 10-second broadcast ident.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright BBC

title: Adobe Creative Cloud — ident
description: The Creative Cloud infinity mark transforms through many styles: chrome liquid, collage, flowers, linework and gradients on black.
why_top_tier: Many contributors' styles orchestrated into one fluid logo journey.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Adobe

title: Australian Open — campaign
description: Bold illustrated tennis: a player under fireworks, an isometric stadium, a dragon-like ball, sunny fan scenes and electric-green splashes. Saturated blue, yellow and coral.
why_top_tier: Gives a grand slam a full illustrative identity with energetic animation.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Tennis Australia

title: The New Yorker Festival 2020
description: Gestural brush and cut-paper shapes in cobalt, green, yellow and red become the Chrysler Building, taxis and subway windows. Poster-like flat composition.
why_top_tier: Event branding in painterly cut-paper motion, a poster brought to life.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Condé Nast / The New Yorker

title: TEDxSydney — titles and identity
description: A tile-pattern system: harlequin diamonds, dot grids and geometric fragments in sand, coral, slate blue and black build crowds and scenery.
why_top_tier: Pattern-based conference identity where every tile can animate; strong system design.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright TEDxSydney

title: Kurzgesagt — climate explainers
description: Flat-vector isometric worlds explaining climate solutions: traffic, food emissions, wind farms and charts, bird characters around graphs. Saturated cyan, purple and green.
why_top_tier: The definitive 2D science explainer style: dense information made friendly with perfect shape language.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Kurzgesagt GmbH

title: Kurzgesagt — Europe's Next Ice Age (Short)
description: A vertical climate short: map of Europe, a mammoth, scientist characters, bold type stacked in the 9:16 frame.
why_top_tier: Kurzgesagt's explainer craft reformatted natively for vertical.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Kurzgesagt GmbH

title: Infinity
description: An endless generative procession of walking figures made of fur, ribbons and particles on black.
why_top_tier: A landmark code-driven artwork; every frame is unique yet art-directed.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Universal Everything

title: BBC Sport — World Cup 2014 titles
description: Brazilian street art comes alive: painted murals, a mural portrait of a player, a footballer figure in rain of colour.
why_top_tier: Painterly sports broadcast opener mixing CG and street art.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright BBC

title: ESPN Monday Night Football — graphics package
description: Player portraits in dramatic light with repeating triptychs and a chrome MNF shield in a stadium of light.
why_top_tier: Contemporary sports broadcast package with high finish.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright ESPN / NFL

title: DEMO Festival — trailer
description: DEMO, a festival of motion design on station screens: bold letters on platform screens, liquid 3D glyphs and a red name card.
why_top_tier: The world's largest motion festival identity, by a leading type-in-motion studio.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright Studio Dumbar/DEPT

title: BBC Two — idents (vertical social cut)
description: Vertical versions of the BBC Two ident: close, dense piles of textured foam, rubber and metal shapes in teal, coral, green and silver with the BBC Two wordmark low in frame.
why_top_tier: The same tactile ident system recomposed natively for portrait screens.
licence: fair-use thumbnail for internal evaluation; copyright BBC
